source_material.description: KESPA V2.3 lock-in / autonomous-learning engineering and Jira update supplied by the project owner on 2026-09-24.

directly_recorded_facts: The autonomous-learning subsystem can initiate research work without an active user.
The curriculum contained 24 enabled research domains at the recorded checkpoint.
A daily operating-system timer was installed and enabled, with a default cycle described as approximately 02:00.
Background lifecycle workers were scheduled on an approximately five-minute cadence.
The first zero-user daily-learning run completed and queued four public research requests.
A maximum verification-age ceiling of 30 days was active as an additional safeguard.
Benchmark gaps may feed research targets without exporting benchmark prompt/gold content into the research pipeline.
Automatic public research publication was hard-disabled.
Blind Trusted Knowledge promotion was hard-disabled.
The lock-in readiness audit reported zero failures, one warning, and PASS WITH WARNINGS.
The remaining audit warning was that external S3-compatible artifact storage was not configured while local encrypted storage remained active.
validation_boundary: The source states that the first production run demonstrates scheduler, persistence, and queue initiation, but does not prove every research request completes every downstream lifecycle stage.
The source does not provide a verified knowledge-card promotion count for the first run.
The source does not provide a research completion rate, verification pass rate, conflict rate, or provider-cost total for the first run.
Bulk curriculum import, the dedicated Learning Operations dashboard, large-scale expansion, and general chat-derived learning sanitization remain future work.
Some pause and audit controls are expressed as operational requirements/expectations rather than all being explicitly verified as deployed UI features.

deduplication.distinct_scope: This release records zero-user curriculum-driven research initiation, recurring OS scheduling, benchmark-gap feeding, and evidence-gated safety boundaries rather than republishing the earlier user-triggered natural research-gap or Trusted Knowledge lifecycle work.

publication_exclusions: credentials, API keys, tokens, cookies, or sessions
raw internal logs and error bodies
unsupported claims that queued research became Trusted Knowledge
unsupported claims of large-scale autonomous-learning performance
